me:2018:q9.question: For a two-dimentional incompressible flow field given by $\vec{u}=A(x\hat{i}-y\hat{j})$ , where $A > 0$ which one of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Its streamlines are given by x = y.

primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown:
C is the false statement

2D incompressible flow continuity equation.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} &=0 \\ \frac{\partial(A x)}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial(-A y)}{\partial y} &=0 \end{aligned}$$

A-A=0 it satisfies continuity equation.

$\Rightarrow A S \quad \vec{V}=A x \hat{i}-A y \hat{j}$

As $y \rightarrow \infty$ velocity vector field will not be defined along y axis.

So flow will be along x-axis i.e. 1 -D flow.

$\Rightarrow$ Stream line equation for $2 \mathrm{D}$

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{d x}{u} &=\frac{d y}{v} \\ \frac{d x}{A x} &=\frac{d y}{-A y} \\ \ln x &=-\ln y+\ln c \\ \ln x y &=\ln c \\ x y &=c \rightarrow \text { streamline equation } \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

detailed_solution.markdown: Let free jet velocity is x displacement $t=\frac{x}{v}$ As per Torricelli's formula, $V=\sqrt{2 g h}$ $t=\frac{x}{\sqrt{2 g h}} \qquad \ldots(i)$ By second law of motion equation $$\begin{aligned} s&=u t+\frac{1}{2} g t^{2} \\ \text{For free fall}\quad u&=0, s=\frac{1}{2} g t^{2}\\ t&=\sqrt{\frac{2 S}{g}} \quad \ldots(ii) \\ \text{ is the time of free fall of object} \end{aligned}$$ By equation (i) and (ii) $$\begin{aligned} \frac{x}{\sqrt{2 g h}} &=\sqrt{\frac{2 s}{g}} \\ x &=\sqrt{4 h s}=\sqrt{4 \times 0.5 \times 0.5}=1 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2018:q34.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 34
me:2018:q34.question: In a Lagrangian system, the position of a fluid particle in a flow is described as $x=x_{o}e^{-kt}$ and $y=y_{o}e^{kt}$ where t is the time while $x_{o}$  ,$x_{o}$, and k are constants. The flow is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$x$ direction scalar of velocity field,

$$\begin{array}{l} u=\frac{d x}{d t} \\ u=-k x_{0}  e^{-k t} \end{array}$$

$y$ direction scalar of velocity field

$$\begin{aligned} v&=\frac{d y}{d t}\\ v &=k y_{0} e^{k t}  \end{aligned}$$

u & v are non zero scalar $t \geq 0$. So the fluid has its motion in both x and y direction indicating 2-dimensional flow.

Now if we carefully see $'u'$ and $'v'$ functions.

$'u'$ can be expressed as $u=-kx$ as $x=x_{0}  e^{-k t}$

$'v'$ can be expressed as $v=ky$ as $y=y_{0}  e^{k t}$

So both $'u'$ and $'v'$ are the function of positions only.

$$\begin{aligned} \vec{V} &=u \hat{i}+v \hat{j} \\ V &=-k x \hat{i}+k y \hat{j}  \end{aligned}$$

So, flow is steady.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2018:q35.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 35
me:2018:q35.question: The maximum reduction in cross-sectional area per pass ( R ) of a cold wire drawing process is $R=1-e^{-(n+1)}$ where n represents the strain hardening coefficient. For the case of a perfectly plastic  material, R is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\sigma_{d}=\sigma_{0} \ln \frac{A_{0}}{A_{f}}$

For maximum reduction

$$\begin{aligned} \sigma_{d} &=\sigma_{0} \\ \sigma_{0} &=\sigma_{0} \ln \frac{A_{0}}{A_{f, \min }} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad 1&=\ln \left(\frac{A_{0}}{A_{f, \min }}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \frac{A_{0}}{A_{f, \min }} &=e=2.71828 \end{aligned}$$

Maximum reduction in Area

$R=\frac{A_{0}-A_{f, \min }}{A_{0}}=\left(1-\frac{1}{e}\right)=\left(1-\frac{1}{2.71828}\right)=0.632$

me:2018:q40.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 40

No damping $\Rightarrow c=0 \Rightarrow \xi=0$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Transmissibility}\quad \epsilon&=\frac{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{2 \xi \omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}}}{\sqrt{\left\{1-\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}\right\}^{2}+\left\{\frac{2 \xi \omega}{\omega_{n}}\right\}^{2}}} \qquad (\xi=0)\\ &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left\{1-\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}\right\}^{2}}} \\ &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left\{1-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}\right\}^{2}}}\\ &=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{1}{\frac{3}{4}}=\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \\ \epsilon&=\frac{F_{t}}{F_{0}} \frac{3}{4}&=\frac{F_t}{50} \\

F_t&=\frac{200}{3}=66.666N\\

&\text{Force from each mount}\\

&=\frac{F_t}{2}=\frac{66.666}{2}=33.333N\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **33.25** (acceptable range: [33, 33.5]).

me:2018:q41.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 41
me:2018:q41.question: A slider crank mechanism is shown in the figure. At some instant, the crank angle is $45^{\circ}$ and a force of 40 N is acting towards the left on the slider. detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Machine - Dynamic Analysis of Slider-crank
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} 30 \sin 45^{\circ} &=70 \sin \beta \\ \sin \beta &=\frac{30 \sin 45}{70}=0.303045 \\ \beta &=17.6406^{\circ} \\ F_{C} \cos \beta &=40 \\ F_{C} &=\frac{40}{\cos \beta}=41.9737 \mathrm{N} \\ F_{t} &=F_{C} \sin (\theta+\beta) \\ &=41.9737 \times \sin \left(17.6406^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right) \\ F_{t} &=37.2785 \mathrm{N} \\ T &=F_{t} \times r=47.2785 \times 0.030 \\ &=1.1183 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m}=1.118 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m} \\ &=1.12 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1.1** (acceptable range: [1, 1.2]).

me:2018:q42.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 42
me:2018:q42.question:
A sprinkler shown in the figure rotates about its hinge point in a horizontal plane due to water flow discharged through its two exit nozzles.

The total flow rate Q through the sprinkler is 1 litre/sec and the cross-sectional area of each exit nozzle is $1 cm^{2}$. Assuming equal flow rate through both arms and a frictionless hinge, the steady state angular speed of rotation (in rad/s) of the sprinkler is ______ (correct to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown: Relative velocities of water with sprinkler $$\begin{aligned} V_{A}&=\frac{Q / 2}{A}=\frac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{2 \times 10^{-4}}=5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{B}&=5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$ Absolute velocity from B side $$\begin{aligned} V_{\text {Abs }}^{\prime}-\left(+r_{B} \omega\right)&=V_{B}\\ V_{A b s}^{\prime} &=V_{B}+r_{B} \omega \\ &=5+0.1 \omega \end{aligned}$$ Absolute velocity from A side $$\begin{aligned} V_{\mathrm{Abs}}-\left(-r_{A} \omega\right)&=V_{A}\\ V_{\mathrm{Abs}}&=V_{A}-r_{A} \omega \\ V_{\mathrm{Abs}}&=5-0.2 \mathrm{c} \end{aligned}$$ The external torque to the sprinkler is zero. $$\begin{aligned} \text{So,}\qquad \Sigma T&=0\\ \dot{m}_{A} V_{A b s} r_{A}-\dot{m}_{B} V_{A b s}^{\prime} r_{B}&=0 \\ \rho\left(\frac{Q}{2}\right)\{5-0.2 \omega\} 0.2-\rho \frac{Q}{2}\{5+0.1 \omega\} 0.1&=0 \\ 1-0.04 \omega-0.5-0.01 \omega&=0 \\ 0.05 \omega&=0.5 \\ \omega&=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **10** (acceptable range: [9.5, 10.5]).

me:2018:q44.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 44
me:2018:q44.question:
A tank of volume 0.05 $m^{3}$ contains a mixture of saturated water and saturated steam at $200^{\circ}C$ . The mass of the liquid present is 8 kg. The entropy (in kJ/kg K) of the mixture is ___________ (correct to two decimal places).

Property data for saturated steam and water are:
At $200^{\circ}C$ , $p_{sat}$ = 1.5538 MPa
$v_{f}$ = 0.001157 $m^{3}$ /kg, $v_{g}$ = 0.12736 $m^{3}$ /kg
$s_{fg}$ =4.1014 kJ/kg K, $s_{f}$= 2.3309 kJ/kg K

primary.subtopicLabel: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
detailed_solution.markdown: Total volume of tank (V) = 0.05 m3 Means of liquid ($m_{2}$) = 8 kg $$\begin{aligned} x &=\frac{m_{v}}{m_{v}+m_{L}}(\text { dryness fraction }) \\ V &=V_{L}+v_{v} \\ \text{where, } &V_{L}-\text{ liquid in tank} \\&V_{v} - \text{ vapour in tank}\\ V_{V} &=m_{v} v_{v} \\ v_{v} &=v_{g} @ 200^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ &=0.12736 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg} \\ V_{V} &=m_{L} v_{L} \\ v_{L} &=v_{f} @ 200^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ &=0.001157 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg} \\ V_{L} &=8 \times 0.001157=9.256 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ 0.05 &=9.256 \times 10^{-3}+\mathrm{V}_{V} \\ V_{V} &=0.0474 \mathrm{m}^{3}\\ \text{So,}\qquad 0.04074 &=m_{v} \times 0.12736 \\ m_{v} &=0.3198 \mathrm{kg} \\ x &=\frac{0.3198}{0.3198+8} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x &=0.0384 \end{aligned}$$ Specific entropy of mixture(s) $$\begin{aligned} s&=s_{f}+x s_{f g} \\ s&=2.3309+0.0384 \times 4.1014 \\ s&=2.4884 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **2.5** (acceptable range: [2.45, 2.55]).

me:2018:q45.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 45
me:2018:q45.question: Steam flows through a nozzle at a mass flow rate of $\dot{m}=0.1$ kg/s with a heat loss of 5 kW. The enthalpies at inlet and exit are2500kJ/kg and 2350 kJ/kg, respectively. Assuming negligible velocity at inlet ($C_{1}\approx 0$ ), the velocity ( $C_{2}$ ) of steam (in m/s) at the nozzle exit is __________ (correct to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown: $\dot{m}=0.1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}, \dot{Q}=5 \mathrm{kW} \text { (heat loss) }$ Applying SFEE $$\begin{aligned} \dot{m}\left(h_{1}+\frac{1}{2} c_{1}^{2}+g z_{1}\right)+\dot{Q}&=\dot{m}\left(h_{2}+\frac{1}{2} c_{2}^{2}+g z_{2}\right)+\dot{w}_{c v}\\ c_{1}=0 \text{ and }\dot{w}_{c v}&=0 \\ z_{1} &=z_{2}(\text { assume }) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \dot{m} h_{1}+\dot{Q} &=\dot{m} h_{2}+\dot{m} \frac{1}{2} c_{2}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.1 \times \frac{1}{2} c_{2}^{2} \times 10^{-3} &=0.1(2500-2350)-5 \\ c_{2} &=447.213 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **447.5** (acceptable range: [445, 450]).

me:2018:q46.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 46
me:2018:q46.question: An engine working on air standard Otto cycle is supplied with air at 0.1 MPa and $35^{\circ}C$. The compression ratio is 8.  The heat supplied is 500 kJ/kg.   Property data for air: $c_{p}$ = 1.005 kJ/kg K, $c_{v}$ = 0.718 kJ/kg K, R = 0.287 kJ/kg K. The maximum temperature (in K) of the cycle is _________ (correct to one decimal place).

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{array}{c} P_{1}=0.1 \mathrm{MPa}, T_{1}=35^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=308 \mathrm{K} \\ \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}=n=8 \\ Q_{s}=500 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ c_{p}=1.005 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ c_{v}=0.718 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ R=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \gamma=\frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}=1.399 \simeq 1.40 \\ T_{3}=T_{\max }=? \end{array}$$ For process 1-2 $$\begin{aligned} P_{1} V_{1}^{\gamma} &=P_{2} V_{2}^{\gamma} \\ P_{2} &=P_{1}\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma}=0.1 \times(8)^{1.4} \\ P_{2} &=1.8379 \mathrm{MPa}\\ \text{and}\qquad \frac{P_{1} V_{1}}{T_{1}} &=\frac{P_{2} V_{2}}{T_{2}} \Rightarrow T_{2} \frac{P_{2} V_{2}}{P_{1} V_{1}} T_{1} \\ T_{2} &=\frac{1.8379 \times 1}{0.1 \times 8} \times 308 \\ T_{2} &=707.6 \mathrm{K}\\ \text{For process } 2 \rightarrow 3 \\ Q_{s}&=C_{V}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right)=500 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}\\ 0.718\left(T_{3}-707.6\right) &=500 \\ T_{3} &=1403.97 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1404** (acceptable range: [1402, 1406]).

me:2018:q49.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 49
me:2018:q49.question: An orthogonal cutting operation is being carried out in which uncut thickness is 0.010 mm, cutting speed is 130 m/min, rake angle is $15^{\circ}$  and width of cut is 6 mm. It is observed that the chip thickness is 0.015 mm, the cutting force is 60 N and the thrust force is 25 N. The ratio of friction energy to total energy is __________ (correct to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} t &=0.010 \mathrm{mm} \\ v &=130 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} \\ \alpha &=15^{\circ} \\ b &=6 \mathrm{mm} \\ t_{c} &=0.015 \mathrm{mm} \\ F_{c} &=60 \mathrm{N} \\ F_{t} &=25 \mathrm{N} \\ F &=F_{c} \sin \alpha+F_{t} \cos \alpha \\ &=60 \sin 15+25 \cos 15=39.6773 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$

Ratio of frictional energy to total energy

$$\begin{array}{l} =\frac{F}{F_{C}} \cdot \frac{V_{C}}{V}=\frac{F}{F_{C}}\left(\frac{t}{t_{C}}\right) \qquad \left[\therefore \; \frac{t}{t_{C}}=\frac{V_{C}}{V}=r \right] \\ =\frac{39.6773}{60} \times \frac{0.010}{0.015}=0.4408 \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.44** (acceptable range: [0.39, 0.49]).

me:2018:q51.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 51

detailed_solution.markdown: $Z=3 x+5 y$ Let us consider $3 x+5 y \leq 15 \qquad \ldots(i)$ $$\begin{aligned} \text { If }\quad 3 x+5 y&=15 \\ x &=0 y=3 \\ x &=5 y=0 \end{aligned}$$ Let us consider $4 x+9 y \leq 8 \qquad \ldots(ii)$ $$\begin{aligned} \text { If } \quad 4 x+9 y &=8 \\ x &=0 y= \frac{8}{9} \\ x &=2 y =0 \end{aligned}$$ Let us consider $13 x+2 y \leq 2 \qquad \ldots(iii)$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{If}\quad 3 x+2 y &=2 \\ x &=0 y=1 \\ x &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} y=0 \end{aligned}$$ Comparing (ii) and (iii) $$\begin{array}{r} 4 x+9 y=8 \qquad \ldots(ii)\\ 13 x+2 y=2 \qquad \ldots(iii)\end{array}$$ From(ii) $\qquad x=\frac{8-9 y}{4}$ Putting in (iii) $\frac{13(8-9 y)}{4}+2 y=2$ $$\begin{aligned} 104-117 y+8 y &=8 \\ 109 y &=96\\ \therefore \quad y=0.88 \\ x=0.02 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, Checking at corner points: $$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad Z\left(0, \frac{8}{9}\right) &=3(0)+5\left(\frac{8}{9}\right)=4.44 \\ Z(0.02,0.88) &=3(0.02)+5(0.88)=4.46 \\ Z\left(\frac{2}{13}, 0\right) &=3\left(\frac{2}{13}\right)+5(0)=0.46 \end{aligned}$$ At (0, 0) Z=0 so minimum value will be 0 Therefore, the correct answer is **0**.

me:2018:q55.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | Question: 55
me:2018:q55.question: An electrochemical machining (ECM) is to be used to cut a through hole into a 12 mm thick aluminum plate. The hole has a rectangular cross-section, $10 mm \times 30 mm$. The ECM operation will be accomplished in 2 minutes, with efficiency of 90%. Assuming specific removal rate for aluminum as $3.44 \times 10^{-2} mm^{3}/(As)$ , the current (in A)  required is __________ (correct to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
Volume of metal to be removed

$$\begin{aligned} &=(10 \times 30) \times 12 \mathrm{mm}^{3}=3600 \mathrm{mm}^{3} \\ \text { Ideal energy required } &=\frac{3600 \mathrm{mm}^{3}}{3.44 \times 10^{-2} \frac{\mathrm{mm}^{3}}{(\mathrm{A} s)}}=104651.163 \mathrm{As} \\ \text { Actual energy required } &=\frac{104651.163}{0.9} \mathrm{As} \\ &=116279.07 \mathrm{As} \\ \text { Time is } 2 \mathrm{min} &=120 \mathrm{s} \\ \therefore \qquad \text { Current }&=\frac{116279.07}{120} \mathrm{A}=968.992 \mathrm{A} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **969** (acceptable range: [968.8, 969.2]).

me:2018:ga:q1.question:
"Going by the _____ that many hands make light work, the school ____ involved all the students in the task."
The words that best fill the blanks in the above sentence are

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Sentence Analysis:** *"Going by the _____ that many hands make light work, the school ____ involved all the students in the task."*
- **Principle** refers to a fundamental truth, proposition, rule, or guiding moral doctrine (such as the proverb *"many hands make light work"*).
- **Principal** refers to the head of a school, college, or chief administrative executive.
- Therefore, the first blank requires **principle** (guiding rule) and the second blank requires **principal** (head of the school).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option A (principle, principal)**.

me:2018:ga:q2.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 2
me:2018:ga:q2.question:
"Her _____ should not be confused with miserliness; she is ever willing to assist those in need."
The word that best fills the blank in the above sentence is

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Miserliness** refers to extreme stinginess or an unwillingness to spend money, even when necessary or to help others.
- The sentence presents an explicit contrast: *"Her _____ should not be confused with miserliness; she is ever willing to assist those in need."*
- The second clause explains that she is generous and ready to help people in need, so her careful spending must not be misconstrued as stinginess.
- **Frugality** means being prudent and economical in consumption and spending without being ungenerous.
- The other options (**cleanliness**, **punctuality**, **greatness**) do not relate to financial prudence, spending habits, or miserliness.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (frugality)**.

me:2018:ga:q3.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 3
me:2018:ga:q3.question: Seven machines take 7 minutes to make 7 identical toys. At the same rate, how many minutes would it take for 100 machine to make 100 toys?

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Unit Rate Analysis:**
  - 7 machines take 7 minutes to make 7 identical toys.
  - This means 1 machine takes 7 minutes to make 1 toy (since $7 \text{ machines} \times 7 \text{ minutes} = 49 \text{ machine-minutes}$ for 7 toys, or $7 \text{ machine-minutes per toy}$).
- **Evaluating 100 Machines:**
  - Each individual machine works independently in parallel.
  - In 7 minutes, each of the 100 machines will produce exactly 1 toy.
  - Therefore, all 100 machines working together will produce $100 \times 1 = 100$ toys in exactly **7 minutes**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (7)**.

me:2018:ga:q4.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 4
me:2018:ga:q4.question: A rectangle becomes a square when its length and breadth are reduced by $10m$ and $5m$, respectively. During this process, the rectangle loses $650m^2$ of area. What is the area of the original rectangle in square meters?

detailed_solution.markdown:
- Let the side of the resulting square be $s$.
- The length and breadth of the original rectangle are:
  $$L = s + 10, \quad B = s + 5$$
- The area of the original rectangle is:
  $$A_1 = L \times B = (s + 10)(s + 5) = s^2 + 15s + 50$$
- The area of the square is $A_2 = s^2$.
- The reduction in area is given as $650 \text{ m}^2$:
  $$A_1 - A_2 = 650 \implies (s^2 + 15s + 50) - s^2 = 650$$
  $$15s + 50 = 650 \implies 15s = 600 \implies s = 40\text{ m}$$
- Original dimensions:
  $$L = 40 + 10 = 50\text{ m}, \quad B = 40 + 5 = 45\text{ m}$$
- Area of the original rectangle:
  $$\text{Area} = 50 \times 45 = 2250\text{ m}^2$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (2250)**.

me:2018:ga:q5.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 5
me:2018:ga:q5.question: A number consists of two digits. The sum of the digits is 9. If 45 is subtracted from the number, its digits are interchanged. What is the number?

detailed_solution.markdown:
- Let the two-digit number be represented as $10x + y$, where $x$ is the tens digit and $y$ is the units digit.
- **Condition 1 (Sum of digits is 9):**
  $$x + y = 9 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$
- **Condition 2 (Subtracting 45 reverses digits):**
  $$(10x + y) - 45 = 10y + x$$
  $$9x - 9y = 45 \implies x - y = 5 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$
- **Solving the system:**
  - Adding (1) and (2): $2x = 14 \implies x = 7$.
  - Substituting $x = 7$ into (1): $y = 9 - 7 = 2$.
- The original number is $10(7) + 2 = 72$.
- Verification: $72 - 45 = 27$, whose digits are the reverse of $72$.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (72)**.

me:2018:ga:q6.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 6
me:2018:ga:q6.question: For integers, $a, b \text{ and } c$, what would be the minimum and maximum values respectively of $a+b+c  \text{  if  } \log a + \log b + \log c=0$?

detailed_solution.markdown:
- Given logarithmic condition:
  $$\log a + \log b + \log c = 0 \implies \log(|a| \cdot |b| \cdot |c|) = 0$$
  $$|a| \cdot |b| \cdot |c| = 1$$
- Since $a, b, c$ are integers, their magnitudes must satisfy $|a| = 1, |b| = 1, |c| = 1$.
- Thus, each variable can take values from $\{-1, 1\}$.
- **Minimum Value:**
  $$a + b + c = (-1) + (-1) + (-1) = -3$$
- **Maximum Value:**
  $$a + b + c = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3$$
- Thus, the minimum and maximum values respectively are **-3 and 3**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option A (-3 and 3)**.

me:2018:ga:q7.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 7
me:2018:ga:q7.question: Given that $a \text{ and }b$ are integers and $a+a^2b^3$ is odd, which of the following statements is correct?
options: a and b are both odd
a and b are both even
a is even and b is odd
a is odd and b is even

detailed_solution.markdown:
- Given expression:
  $$E = a + a^2 b^3 = a(1 + a b^3)$$
- We are given that $E$ is **odd**.
- For the product of two integers to be odd, **both factors must be odd**:
  1. $a$ must be **odd**.
  2. $(1 + a b^3)$ must be **odd**.
- For $(1 + a b^3)$ to be odd, the term $a b^3$ must be **even** (since $\text{even} + 1 = \text{odd}$).
- Since $a$ is already established to be odd:
  $$\text{odd} \times b^3 = \text{even} \implies b^3 \text{ must be even} \implies b \text{ must be even}.$$
- Thus, $a$ is odd and $b$ is even.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D (a is odd and b is even)**.

me:2018:ga:q8.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 8
me:2018:ga:q8.question: From the time the front of a train enters a platform, it takes 25 seconds for the back of the train to leave the platform, while traveling at a constant speed of 54 km/h. At the same speed, it takes 14 seconds to pass a man running at 9 km/h in the same direction as the train. What is the length of the train and that of the platform in meters, respectively?

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Speed Conversions:**
  - Train speed $v_T = 54\text{ km/h} = 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15\text{ m/s}$.
  - Man's running speed $v_M = 9\text{ km/h} = 9 \times \frac{5}{18} = 2.5\text{ m/s}$.
- **Finding Train Length ($L_T$):**
  - Relative speed when train passes the man in the same direction:
    $$v_{\text{rel}} = v_T - v_M = 15 - 2.5 = 12.5\text{ m/s}$$
  - The train completely passes the man in 14 seconds:
    $$L_T = v_{\text{rel}} \times t = 12.5 \times 14 = 175\text{ meters}$$
- **Finding Platform Length ($L_P$):**
  - From the front entering until the back leaves, total distance traversed is $L_T + L_P$:
    $$L_T + L_P = v_T \times 25\text{ s} = 15 \times 25 = 375\text{ meters}$$
    $$L_P = 375 - 175 = 200\text{ meters}$$
- Thus, train length is $175\text{ m}$ and platform length is $200\text{ m}$.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D (175 and 200)**.

me:2018:ga:q9.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 9
me:2018:ga:q9.question: Which of the following functions describe the graph shown in the below figure?

detailed_solution.markdown:
- We test the function $y = ||x| - 1| - 1$ at key critical points:
  - At $x = 0$:
    $$y = ||0| - 1| - 1 = |-1| - 1 = 1 - 1 = 0$$
  - At $x = 1$ and $x = -1$:
    $$y = ||\pm 1| - 1| - 1 = |0| - 1 = -1$$
    This yields local minima at $(1, -1)$ and $(-1, -1)$.
  - At $x = 2$ and $x = -2$:
    $$y = ||\pm 2| - 1| - 1 = |1| - 1 = 0$$
    These are the roots where the graph crosses the x-axis.
  - For $|x| > 2$:
    $$y = (|x| - 1) - 1 = |x| - 2$$
    This produces linear rays of slope $\pm 1$.
- This describes the symmetric double-V (W-shaped) curve passing through $(0,0)$ with minima at $(\pm 1, -1)$ and roots at $\pm 2$.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B ($y=||x|-1|-1$)**.

me:2018:ga:q10.title: GATE ME 2018 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 10
me:2018:ga:q10.question:
Consider the following three statements:

i. Some roses are red.
ii. All red flowers fade quickly.
iii. some roses fade quickly.

Which of the following statements can be logically inferred from the above statements?
options: If (i) is true and (ii) is false, then (iii) is false.
If (i) is true and (ii) is false, then (iii) is true.
If (i) and (ii) are true, then (iii) is true.
If (i) and (ii) are false, then (iii) is false.

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Given Statements:**
  - (i) *Some roses are red.* $\implies \{ \text{roses} \} \cap \{ \text{red flowers} \} \neq \emptyset$.
  - (ii) *All red flowers fade quickly.* $\implies \{ \text{red flowers} \} \subseteq \{ \text{things that fade quickly} \}$.
  - (iii) *Some roses fade quickly.*
- **Logical Deduction:**
  - Since some roses belong to the set of red flowers (from i), and all red flowers belong to the set of things that fade quickly (from ii), those particular roses must also fade quickly.
  - Therefore, whenever both (i) and (ii) are true, statement (iii) is guaranteed to be true.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (If (i) and (ii) are true, then (iii) is true.)**.
